# Parity Test Fixtures

These three images back the browser↔Node pixel-parity test
(`packages/nukebg-core/tests/parity/parity.test.ts`, REQ-PARITY-1 /
REQ-PARITY-4 in `openspec/changes/extract-core-cli/specs/browser-app-parity.md`).

## They are SYNTHETIC placeholders

| File | Stands in for | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `portrait-512x512.png` | Human portrait, white background | Deterministic filled ellipse ("skin tone" solid color) on a solid white background |
| `product-800x600.jpg` | Product photo with watermark | Deterministic filled ellipse ("product body") on a light background, with a repeating diagonal semi-transparent stripe pattern baked into the RGB (watermark stand-in — JPEG has no alpha channel) |
| `logo-256x256.png` | Icon/logo, transparent background | Deterministic opaque circle on a fully transparent background |

They are generated by pure math (no photographs, no external assets, no
randomness) via
`packages/nukebg-cli/scripts/generate-parity-fixtures.mjs`. Re-running that
script reproduces byte-identical files. This keeps the fixtures
license-free and committable without sourcing real photography.

## Why not real images

Sourcing licensed, representative portrait/product/logo photography for a
test fixture set is out of scope for this change and was not available in
the environment that implemented Phase 17. The synthetic fixtures are
"good enough" to exercise the pipeline's code paths (subject detection,
background classification, watermark stripe pattern) and to keep the
comparison math (`packages/nukebg-core/src/parity/compare-alpha.ts`) unit
tested today.

## What CI still needs (Phase 18)

Real perceptual parity enforcement — i.e., actually asserting that
`WorkerPipelineRunner` (browser) and `NodePipelineRunner` (Node) produce
matching alpha channels on realistic photography — requires BOTH:

1. Realistic fixture images (real portraits/products/logos with an
   appropriate license for redistribution in this repo), and
2. Cached RMBG/LaMa models in the CI job (see tasks.md X.6 and Phase 18),
   with `NUKEBG_PARITY_REQUIRE=1` set only on the leg that has the cache
   populated.

Until both are in place, `parity.test.ts` skips its end-to-end assertions
locally (and in any CI leg without `NUKEBG_PARITY_REQUIRE=1`) with the
message defined in REQ-PARITY-4. The epsilon/threshold comparison logic
itself (`compare-alpha.ts`) is unit tested independently of models or
fixtures and is green today.
